# Three durable comments credit a pre-push guard this repository does not have

## Context

Measured while taking #18757's first decision ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18757#issuecomment-5702289441)). That ticket's **AC-3** names one stale claim; reading the neighbourhood found two more of the same kind, in the guard that sits beside them.

`check-commit-authorship.mjs` lives in `neo-agent-brain` and this repository does not depend on it — the only agent dependency is `neo-agent-skills`. Three durable comments here describe it as a caller in this tree anyway.

Live latest-open sweep 2026-09-16T14:20Z — latest 20 open issues plus a search on the guard's name: only #18757 (parent) and #17171. A2A sweep of the latest 30 messages: no competing claim.

## The Problem

| site | claim | measured |
|---|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/spec-retirement-lint.yml:22` | *"The two existing pre-push guards (check-branch-discipline, **check-commit-authorship**) are hook-only"* | `.husky/pre-push` runs `check-branch-discipline` and **`check-spec-retirement`**. The named guard is not on this hook; the one that is, is missing from the sentence |
| `buildScripts/util/check-spec-retirement.mjs:23` | *"`check-commit-authorship.mjs` reads commit messages from **the same hook** for the same reason"* | there is no such file in this repository and it is on no hook here |
| `buildScripts/util/check-spec-retirement.mjs:72` | *"Same contract as `check-commit-authorship.mjs`, whose comment records why…"* | the **provenance is true** — this guard's range handling was lifted from it — but the pointer reads as a sibling in this tree |
| `buildScripts/util/check-spec-retirement.mjs:321` | `RA-3:` prefixing the survivor-matching rule | review archaeology: CI's published guard flags it, the engine's mirrored copy carries none of those patterns, so the hook passes it (#18809) |

This is the defect class the archaeology guard exists to prevent, one level up: a comment asserting a *relationship* rather than a ticket number, which no guard checks and which decays silently. The first one is the most costly, because it is load-bearing in an argument — it justifies the workflow's coverage claim by counting a guard that is not there.

## The Architectural Reality

The provenance at `:72` is worth keeping and the two coverage claims are not. A comment may say *where a contract came from*; it may not say *what runs here* unless it does. The repair is to make each sentence describe this tree, and to name the out-of-repo guard as out-of-repo where it is genuinely being credited.

## The Fix

Three comments. No behaviour, no code.

1. `spec-retirement-lint.yml:22` — name the guards `.husky/pre-push` actually runs.
2. `check-spec-retirement.mjs:23` — state the pre-push reason on its own terms; the sibling is not on this hook.
3. `check-spec-retirement.mjs:72` — keep the provenance, mark the source as living in `neo-agent-brain`, so a reader does not go looking for it here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: no durable comment in this repository describes `check-commit-authorship` as running here.
- [ ] AC-2: `spec-retirement-lint.yml`'s coverage sentence names the guards on `.husky/pre-push` at HEAD, verified against the hook rather than from memory.
- [ ] AC-3: the `:72` provenance survives, with its source located out-of-repo.
- [ ] AC-4: comment-only — `git diff -U0` carries no changed line outside a comment.

## Out of Scope

- **Wiring the guard** — #18757's AC-1 and AC-2, and its placement decision. This ticket must not read as having settled it: the comments describe today's tree, and land correctly whichever way that decision goes.
- The `--no-verify` / required-context argument the workflow header makes (#17171).

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Do not delete the `:72` provenance.** It records why the range handling looks the way it does, and that reason outlives the guard's location. Only its address is wrong.
- ⛔ **Do not "fix" it by wiring the guard instead.** That is the parent's substance and is blocked on a custody decision; repairing prose must not become a reason to presume it.
- ⛔ **Do not explain these as somebody describing the hook from memory.** They were accurate when written and DECAYED: `efba884dcb` ran `./buildScripts/util/check-commit-authorship.mjs` on the hook — the guard was neo-local then — and `c623b2f63c` deleted that line after it had moved to `ai/`. A comment naming a caller is a claim with an expiry date, and nothing watches it; that is the defect, not carelessness.
- ⛔ **Do not verify the hook from recall.** AC-2 says read `.husky/pre-push` at HEAD — a decayed claim reads exactly like a correct one, which is the whole reason this class survives.
